Answer: F
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates dextrocardia (heart on the right) and a right-sided gastric bubble, confirming situs inversus totalis. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus, the anatomical orientation is mirrored; therefore, bronchiectatic changes are typically more pronounced on the left side (the morphological right lung), which aligns with the findings described in option F.
